title: Phone Stand
lines: A printable stand in eight steps
Ends with an STL for your slicer
say: In this tutorial we'll design a phone stand in OpenShape 3D and get it ready for 3D printing. We'll sketch a side profile, extrude it, round the edges, cut a slot for the charging cable, and export an STL. Everything is done through the touch interface, so you can follow along.

title: A blank design
lines: Undo, views, Items and History on top
say: Start a blank design. The tool palette is on the left, and the toolbar on top has undo, the views, and the Items and History panels.

title: Step 1 · Front plane
sub: Sketch › Line, tap the blue tile
lines: The stand is a side profile, extruded
So we draw it standing up
say: The stand is just a side profile pulled out sideways, so we draw that profile standing up. Tap Sketch, then Line, and pick the blue front-plane tile.

title: Step 2 · The base
say: First the base. Tap once on the left and once on the right for a horizontal line, then tap Line again to finish. The line stays selected: tap its badge and type ninety millimeters. Fit View zooms to match.

title: Step 3 · The back
sub: A vertical line, typed to 60 mm
lines: Start on the left end of the base
Tap up, then Vertical in the constraints panel
say: Now the back. Pick Line, start on the left end of the base, and tap upwards. Finish, then tap Vertical in the constraints panel so it stays upright, type sixty millimeters for the height, and Fit View again so the whole stand fits on screen.

title: Step 4 · The profile
lines: Top of the back, then the slope the phone rests on
The floor, the lip, and down to the base
Finish on the base's right end
say: Now trace the rest. Start at the top of the back, tap the top of the back rest, then down the slope the phone will lean against, along the floor, up and over the front lip, and finish on the right end of the base. The loop closes and fills in.

title: Step 5 · Extrude
say: Exit the sketch and tap inside the filled profile. The Extrude bar appears. Type seventy millimeters, wide enough for any phone, and the profile becomes a solid stand.

title: Step 6 · Material
say: Double-tap the stand to select it, open Material, and pick a preset. Apply. This is only the look; the geometry stays exact.

title: Step 7 · Round the edges
lines: Top view: tap the long edges
say: Let's soften the edges you'll touch. From the top view, tap Modify, then Fillet, and tap the long edges: the front of the lip, and both edges along the top of the back. Type a three millimeter radius and Apply.

title: Step 8 · Cable slot
sub: Sketch on a face, cut through
lines: Sketch › Rectangle, tap the floor face
Drag a rectangle where the cable goes
say: Now a slot for the charging cable. Tap Sketch, then Rectangle, and this time tap the floor of the stand: any flat face works as a sketch plane. Drag a rectangle where the connector sits. Exit the sketch, tap the fill, choose Subtract, and type minus fifteen. The cut goes straight through the floor.

title: Step 9 · Export for printing
lines: Prints flat on its base, no supports
8 mm walls, 3 mm radii: strong and quick
Open the STL in your slicer
say: That's the stand. Open the export menu and choose STL or 3MF for your slicer. It prints flat on its base with no supports, and the eight millimeter walls make it sturdy. Every step is still in History if you want a different angle or a wider slot.

title: Print it
say: OpenShape 3D is free and open source, with no account and no cloud. Thanks for watching, and happy printing.
